candidates.current_role: State Representative, Texas House District 73, since 2023
candidates.background: Isaac represents Comal County and western Hays County. She ran unsuccessfully for House District 45 in 2020, was first elected to District 73 in 2022 and ran unopposed in the 2026 Republican primary. She is married to former Rep. Jason Isaac.

priorities.text: Says property taxes are the top issue she hears from voters.
Says unmanaged growth is straining Hill Country water.
Says school funding should follow the student, reward results and support neighborhood schools and parental choice.
Pledges to cut taxes, give communities local control and uphold the rule of law.

promises.text: Says she will seek a 3 percent cap on homestead appraisals, a two-thirds voter approval requirement for tax increases and state spending limits for local governments.
Says she will refile HB 5325, requiring new plats that rely on groundwater to prove an adequate supply.
Says she will help pass legislation setting parameters for data centers and ending tax breaks that subsidize them.

record.text: Voted for SB 2 (2025), which created the state education savings account program; it passed the House 86 to 61.
Voted for HB 2 (2025), the main public school finance bill, on third reading; it passed 142 to 5.
Voted for the motion to concur in Senate amendments to HB 2 (2025 school finance); it prevailed 122 to 13.
Voted against a 2025 budget amendment by Rep. John Bucy directing the state to seek a federal waiver to expand Medicaid eligibility; it failed 63 to 85.
Voted for SB 17 (2025), restricting land purchases by people and entities tied to certain foreign adversary countries; it passed 86 to 59.
Voted for SJR 5 (2025), a constitutional amendment allowing denial of bail for certain violent offenses; it was adopted 133 to 8.
Voted for SB 9 (2025), changing bail procedures and regulating charitable bail organizations; it passed 118 to 25.
Voted for SB 3 (2025), which would have banned most consumable hemp-derived THC products, on second reading; it advanced 95 to 44.
Voted for SB 33 (2025), barring local governments from funding travel for abortion services; it passed 87 to 58.
Voted for SB 8 (2025), requiring certain sheriffs to seek agreements with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement; it passed 86 to 47.
Voted for SB 10 (2025), requiring Ten Commandments displays in public school classrooms; it passed 82 to 46.
Voted for SB 1362 (2025), prohibiting the recognition and enforcement of extreme risk protective orders; it passed 86 to 53.
Voted for the conference report on SB 1, the 2026-2027 state budget; it was adopted 107 to 21.
Voted for HB 4 (2025 second called session), redrawing Texas congressional districts; it passed 88 to 52.
Voted for HB 7 (2025 second called session), restricting abortion-inducing drugs; it passed 82 to 48.
Voted against a 2023 budget amendment (Amendment No. 45 to HB 1) barring the use of state funds for school vouchers or similar programs; it was adopted 86 to 52.
Voted against the November 2023 amendment offered by Rep. John Raney, Rep. Drew Darby and others that struck the education savings account program from HB 1; it was adopted 84 to 63.
Voted for SB 14 (2023), banning gender transition medical treatments for minors; it passed 87 to 56.
Voted against HR 2377 (2023), impeaching Attorney General Ken Paxton; it was adopted 121 to 23.
Voted for SB 3 (2023 fourth called session), funding state border barrier construction; it passed 84 to 59.
Voted for SB 4 (2023 fourth called session), creating a state offense for illegal entry from a foreign nation; it passed 83 to 61.
Authored HB 5325 (2025) on groundwater supply evidence for subdivision plats, which did not pass, and HB 218 on directing surplus revenue to a fund for reducing school property taxes.
Authored HB 1337 (2025) on recognition of out-of-state handgun licenses and HB 2882 on the definition of short-barrel firearm.

notes.text: Endorsed in the 2024 Republican primary by Gov. Greg Abbott, who backed incumbents who supported his 2023 education savings account bill, according to ATPE.
Endorsed by the Texas Home School Coalition in 2020 and 2022, according to ATPE.

q_vouchers.summary: Voted for SB 2 (2025) and against 2023 amendments blocking voucher funding; says school funding should support parental choice.

q_school_funding.summary: Voted for HB 2, the 2025 school finance bill.

q_ten_commandments.summary: Voted for SB 10 (2025), requiring classroom Ten Commandments displays.

q_medicaid.summary: Voted against a 2025 budget amendment directing the state to seek a waiver to expand Medicaid.

q_bail.summary: Voted for SJR 5 and for SB 9, the 2025 bail measures.

q_cannabis.summary: Voted for SB 3 (2025), which would have banned most hemp-derived THC products.

q_foreign_land.summary: Voted for SB 17 (2025), restricting land purchases tied to designated foreign adversaries.

q_abortion.summary: Voted for SB 33 (2025) and for HB 7 (2025), both measures restricting abortion access.

q_gun_laws.summary: Voted for SB 1362 (2025) and authored 2025 bills on handgun license reciprocity and short-barrel firearm definitions.

q_deportation.summary: Voted for SB 8 (2025), requiring sheriff agreements with ICE; voted for SB 4 (2023), creating a state illegal entry offense. No direct statement on deportation priorities was found.

q_border_state.summary: Voted for SB 3 (2023), which funded state border barrier construction.

q_trans_minors.summary: Voted for SB 14 (2023), the ban on gender transition treatments for minors.

q_prop_tax_eliminate.summary: Says she will fight to have the state fund school maintenance and operations so school taxes no longer fall on homestead owners.

q_spending_cap.summary: Says local governments should live within state spending limits.

issue_notes.summary: Says the Hill Country is not the place for data centers.

candidates.background: Fox is a retired school principal and executive director of Circle Arts Theatre. She ran unopposed in the 2026 Democratic primary for the district, which covers Comal County and western Hays County.

priorities.text: Calls water quality and availability the most significant concern in the district.
Campaigns on tax and rental relief for families.
Campaigns on adequately funding public schools and a transparent accountability system.
Says communities should have a voice in managing growth and development.

promises.text: Says she will work to raise the basic allotment and index it to inflation and oppose vouchers.
Says she will support stronger wastewater standards, county authority to manage growth and groundwater district enforcement against commercial overpumping.
Says she will support requiring large developers to disclose water and energy use and environmental impacts.

notes.text: Endorsed by the Texas AFL-CIO COPE for the 2026 general election.
